description: The short Heritage escape spelling `op` inside an EXECUTED `map` body reports the same canonical `params` `{ keyword: "return", form: "map" }` as `output` and as Core `return` (issue #741) — byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/comprehensions/comprehension-return-in-comprehension` (`:out = map n in [1] [ return :n ]`) in `code`, `params`, `stage` and `severity`. Together with its `output` sibling this pins every Heritage spelling of the second runtime `keyword` site: the defective param varied WITH the spelling, so each spelling needs its own assertion. `source_span` covers the `op :n` escape statement (5 columns against the 9 of `output :n`), so the span still follows the surface spelling while the param does not. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
